channel.title: Wire — Databases
channel.description: Databases from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS “Cinnamon Teal”
item.description: The DuckDB team is happy to announce that today we're releasing DuckDB version 2.0.0 LTS, codenamed “Cinnamon Teal” (Spatula cyanoptera). (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Article: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
item.description: This article presents a disaster-recovery analytics workflow in which an AI agent generates constrained SQL or Python, DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet, and the agent interprets the results. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: I Tried to Find Out How ClickHouse Keeper Takes Non-Blocking Snapshots
item.description: This is a continuation from my previous post here: https://www.reddit.com/r/programming/comments/1x8gk1v/i_traced_a_postgres_insert_to_raw_bytes_on_disk/ I've been putting together some notes/videos/blog posts - partly for my own future… (1 source: rprogramming)

item.title: FOSSASIA PGDay 2027
item.description: Schedule, talks and talk submissions for FOSSASIA PGDay 2027 (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: 84% of surveyed Ruby on Rails developers run Postgres in production
item.description: 📌 Summary 84% of 1,800 surveyed Rails developers use PostgreSQL in production. While PostgreSQL is less popular than Oracle, MySQL, and Microsoft SQL Server today, the gap is shrinking. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: How hstore Can Beat jsonb for Audit Logs
Why is Postgres's numeric Type So Slow?
item.description: Why is PostgreSQL’s numeric type slow? Andrei Lepikhov traces four design decisions behind its cost and compares DuckDB’s DECIMAL to see what exactness takes. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: Citus Hits 10M QPS on Half Neki's Data Nodes
item.description: Open-source Citus delivers millions of queries per second more efficiently than Neki, the only other published data point at this scale (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: 118M QPS Neki post
item.description: We ran a massive, sharded Postgres database at 118.5 million queries per second, with 200k queries per second on each shard across 512 shards. (1 source: postgresweekly)
